For postgres also first_releases (per branch the change landed on: branch, sh

tools.name: find_failing_patches
tools.description: Commitfest entries whose latest cfbot build fails on at least one platform: cf_id, title, entry_status and commitfest_number. entry_status filters (default the active reviewable statuses, e.g. needs-review, ready-for-committer); platform narrows to one CI platform; limit caps the list. Cite https://

tools.name: get_attachment
tools.description: The content of one attachment of a mail message (a patch, a log, a test case), chosen by 1-based index or a filename substring, as listed in get_message/get_thread attachments. Text attachments come back as decoded text (a .patch is ready to read or `git apply`), binary ones as base64 with encoding=

tools.name: get_callers
tools.description: Reverse call graph: the symbols that call or reference qualified_name (from search_symbols), each with its file and lines, like `git grep -w <name>` restricted to call sites. HEAD only; macro expansion and function pointers are not followed. limit caps the list. Read a caller with git_show_file at i

tools.name: get_contributor
tools.description: A contributor's profile by email (exact) or name (substring): canonical name, page hash, totals and per-release counts by role (authored, reviewed, committed, reported, ...), the 5 latest credited commits with sha, and buildfarm animals they own. People who hid their page are excluded from name look

tools.name: get_doc_page
tools.description: One PostgreSQL documentation page as text: path (e.g. "brin.html" or "sql-createtable.html") and optional version ("17", "current"; default the latest). Returns its url, path and stored text (body) with fetched_at. Use search_docs to find the path. Cite the returned url.

tools.name: get_entry
tools.description: One commitfest entry by cf_id (the number in commitfest.postgresql.org/patch/<cf_id>/): title, status, commitfest, authors, reviewers, committer, its mail threads and branches. Read the thread with get_thread; cfbot state with find_failing_patches. Cite https://commitfest.postgresql.org/patch/<cf_id

tools.name: get_message
tools.description: One mail message by Message-ID: headers, in_reply_to/references, decoded body text (by default the author's own words: quotes, signature and inline patch removed; full_text=true for everything, quotes included), attachments [{index, filename, content_type, size}] and has_patch. Never raw MIME: get_a

tools.name: get_thread
tools.description: A mail thread, found by any Message-ID in it, oldest first. Each message: from, to, cc, date, message_id, decoded body text (by default the author's own words: quoted replies, signature and inline patch removed; full_text=true for the whole decoded text; never raw MIME), attachments [{index, filenam

tools.name: get_wiki_page
tools.description: One wiki.postgresql.org page by title: its latest revision content with author and date. Titles are as on the wiki ("Don't Do This", "Todo"). Use search_wiki to find a title, get_wiki_history for older revisions. Cite https://wiki.postgresql.org/wiki/<title>.

tools.name: git_log
tools.description: Commit history like `git log`, newest first, filtered by path (commits touching a file), author (substring), since/until (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC 3339) and branch (any branch, tag or major version such as 17 or 9.6; default the indexed default branch). Each commit: sha (40-hex, cite it), commit_id, messag

tools.name: git_search

Each commit: sha (40-hex, cite it), commit_id, message, author, date, people credited, and mail_refs: up to 5 messages t

tools.name: hybrid_search
tools.description: Mailing-list search, keyword (BM25 over the authors' own words) and semantic (embeddings) blended per thread, over every list unless inbox names one or more. Returns up to limit threads (default 20, max 50), best first, each its best message: inbox, message_id, subject, from, date, thread_id, fused_

tools.name: list_sources
tools.description: Every source behind this server with its kind (inbox, repository, docs, wiki, discord), item count, last update and freshness (fresh/stale): the 56 mailing lists, the git repositories, the documentation releases, the wiki and Discord. Use it to learn the inbox and repository names other tools accept

tools.name: search_commitfest
tools.description: Full-text search of commitfest entries (title first, then author/reviewer/committer names), in the current commitfest by default, or commitfests="all" (back to 2014) or a comma list of numbers. Websearch syntax: "phrase", -term, or. Each result: cf_id, title, status, commitfest(s), people, last upda

tools.name: search
tools.description: Keyword search of mailing-list messages (BM25 over subject, sender and the authors' own words), every list unless inbox narrows it. Operators in query: s:/intitle: subject, f:/from: sender, b:/intext: body, after:/before:/d:2024-01..2025-01 dates, site:<list>, filetype:patch, link:<url glob>, /regex

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Full-text search of the PostgreSQL documentation (websearch syntax: "phrase", -term, or), title matches first. Searches the current release unless version (one, e.g. "17") or versions (several) is given; a page matching in several selected versions is one result listing each version and its URL. Ret

tools.name: search_symbols
tools.description: Find C functions, macros, types and variables by name in the indexed source (HEAD): BM25 on names, then fuzzy and body matches. Filter by kind (function, struct, macro, ...), language, repository. Each result: qualified_name, name, kind, language, file, start_line and end_line. Like `ctags`/`git gre

tools.description: Full-text search (websearch syntax) of wiki.postgresql.org. By default searches each page's current text; history=true searches every revision and returns, per page, the latest matching revision (rev_id, revision_url, author, comment, timestamp, is_current) and how many matched; since/until bound th

tools.name: cross_reference
tools.description: What relates to one stored item, and what happened to it. ref: a Message-ID or message URL, a commit SHA or URL, a docs URL or page.html, a wiki URL or title, a commitfest URL, CVE-YYYY-NNNNN, or feature:<words> (matched to commitfest titles; ref.entries_used says which). Returns related threads, co

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: Catch up: everything a person or group did, and where they were named, in a window, newest first per kind (mail grouped by thread). who: a name (fuzzy; close matches return ambiguous [{name, hash}]), email, hash:<8 hex>, team:<slug>, org:<name>, new:<window>, a phrase ('the core team'), or a list. s

tools.name: code_search
tools.description: Search the postgres source at any commit, branch, tag or date (or across history), from the code-history index: every line of every commit, byte-exact. A literal by default; match=regex for a PostgreSQL regex (^ and $ are per line; \b \< \> as in grep), match=identifier for any of snake_case/CamelCa

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file of the postgres source at any commit, branch, tag or date from the code-history index: numbered lines, at most 2000 per call (page with start_line/end_line), byte-exact to git. Says total_lines and complete; binary files return their metadata only.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List the files of the postgres source under a directory at any commit, branch, tag or date (code-history index), with line counts; depth folds deeper paths into directories with file counts; glob filters paths.

tools.name: blame
tools.description: Per-line blame of a postgres file at any commit (code-history index): the commit that wrote each line, as `git blame` with git's default diff. ignore_revs (default true) passes through the pgindent/reformat commits of .git-blame-ignore-revs when they replaced lines one-for-one; reverse adds the comm

tools.name: get_commit

tools.name: search_commits
tools.description: Search postgres commits (code-history index), newest first, like git log: range (a rev, or A..B; default the newest release branch), message (regex, case-insensitive), author (regex over author, committer and Author/Co-authored-by/Reviewed-by trailers), paths, since/until (YYYY-MM-DD), changed_lines

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: retrieve_context, commit_history, find_failing_patches, get_attachment, get_contributor, get_doc_page, get_entry, get_message, get_thread, git_search, hybrid_search, list_sources, search_commitfest, search, search_docs, search_wiki, cross_reference, whats_new, get_commit, search_commits · Private data: commit_history, get_callers, git_log, git_search, search_symbols, code_search, read_file, list_files, blame, get_commit, search_commits · Public sink: get_contributor, cross_reference, whats_new.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: retrieve_context, commit_history, find_failing_patches, get_attachment, get_contributor, get_doc_page, get_entry, get_message, get_thread, git_search, hybrid_search, list_sources, search_commitfest, search, search_docs, search_wiki, cross_reference, whats_new, get_commit, search_commits · Private data: commit_history, get_callers, git_log, git_search, search_symbols, code_search, read_file, list_files, blame, get_commit, search_commits · Public sink: get_contributor, cross_reference, whats_new

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
